The historic center preserves churches and buildings from the colonial period. Key sites include the Church of Nossa Senhora da Pena, the city museum and memorial sites connected with the Portuguese exploration and settlement of the coast.

The other part of a visit focuses on beaches, reefs and resort facilities. Porto Seguro can be combined with Itacaré, Morro de São Paulo and Salvador for a Bahia itinerary that takes in several different stretches of coastline.

## Portobelo — a window into Panama's colonial era!

This quiet fishing village was once a prosperous city and the largest Spanish port in Central America. Gold from Peru and treasures from the East were brought to Panama City and transported overland by mule to the fortress at Portobelo.

## Portobelo — for lovers of history!

Magnificent examples of colonial architecture remain from the city's former days of grandeur: residential and administrative buildings and churches beautiful enough to grace any city in the country. They have survived despite the repeated attacks and destruction inflicted on the city by English pirates throughout its history. The surrounding area contains the ruins of numerous forts, although several are still entirely intact. One of the city's churches houses a statue of the "Black Christ," which draws thousands of worshippers on pilgrimage every year.

Post Office Bay invites you to take out a postcard and write a few lines by hand. On Floreana Island, amid sand, dark lava and coastal shrubs, stands a postal barrel. Whalers began leaving letters here in 1793, hoping that a ship heading in the right direction would collect them.

The tradition continues today. Travelers leave their own postcards and look through messages from other visitors. If an address lies along your route, you can take the card and deliver it to its recipient. This small act makes the history of seafarers feel very close: your letter, too, will carry on its journey after you return home.

After visiting the post office, it is pleasant to linger by the water. Look at the uneven volcanic rocks, listen to the surf and imagine the long voyages ships once made across the Pacific Ocean. Post Office Bay is especially appealing to visitors interested in the human stories of the Galápagos. A visit adds a personal episode to an island journey where wildlife usually takes center stage.

Potosí is the capital of Bolivia's Potosí Department. It is considered the highest city in the world. The city lies at the foot of Cerro de Potosí, on rich silver deposits that were its main source of livelihood for a long period.

The city's main attractions include the San Francisco convent (now home to the Museum of Religious Art), the Santa Teresa church and convent, Casa de la Moneda (1542, the first mint in Potosí, now the National Museum), the Casa de las Tres Portadas mansion, the "Crystal Palace," San Lorenzo Church, and the churches of Belén, San Bernardo, San Agustín and La Compañía de Jesús.

Beautiful architectural landmarks recall the city's former grandeur: churches and monasteries, grand mansions and other masterpieces of the colonial era. Tours of working mines are of particular interest to visitors. Travelers are taken deep into the mountain and shown how the valuable metal is extracted.

Pozo Azul is tucked away amid Canaima's greenery. A small stream fills the natural pool, and sunlight gives the water a bluish hue. Visitors can linger by the shore after their walk.

A trail leads to the site after a river journey. Pozo Azul is offered both as a separate excursion and in combination with a trek to Curaveina. Whether swimming is possible is agreed with the guide according to conditions on site.
